newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: J.Martins formally announces Vidago bid.
newsitem.headline: J.Martins formally announces Vidago bid.

text.p: Portugal's second biggest retailer Jeronimo Martins has made a preliminary announcement of a public offer to buy (OPA) mineral water company Vidago for 4,300 escudos per share.
The announcement published in today's Publico newspaper said the bid was conditional on Vidago's shareholders selling at least 90 percent of Vidago's capital of 3.7 billion escudos.
Jeronimo Martins said on Saturday it would bid for Vidago, Portugal's leading sparkling water supplier, valuing the company at 15.8 billion escudos.
Jeronimo Martins shares stood at 14,025 escudos, up five, in volume of 100 shares at 1058 GMT.
Trade in shares in drinks group Unicer was halted today by the Lisbon bourse authorities, apparently after a news report that it was preparing a counter-offer for Vidago, dealers said.
Diario Economico newspaper reported that Unicer was interested in bidding for Vidago after Jeronimo Martins said it would launch a bid.

The paper quoted a source close to Unicer, which distributes beer, mineral water, wine and juices, as saying his company was interested in acquiring Vidago, even though it believed the price bid by Jeronimo Martins was too high.
If Unicer offered to buy Vidago, it would have to offer a price that was at least five percent higher than the previous bid, according to Portuguese law.
A Unicer spokesman, contacted by Reuters, declined comment on the company's reported interest in Vidago.
The Financial Markets Committee (CMVM) today ended a 24-hour suspension in trade in Vidago shares on Lisbon bourse.
Vidago shares surged, standing at 4,200 escudos, up 995, in volume of 2,200 shares at 1100 GMT.
